subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an agent turn emits tool-call-shaped assistant text instead of structured toolCall/toolUse content?
rationale: Current main intentionally combines warning-only diagnostics, limited compatibility promotion, and scoped Gateway HTTP enforcement; changing this default affects both the execution security boundary and local-model compatibility.

options.title: Define bounded enforcement
options.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it with focused agent-loop, provider-stream, Gateway, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Document the current behavior as provider/model incompatibility and accept that fake tool-call text can still reach transcripts or visible replies without a real tool call.

options.title: Split response-gate work
options.body: Limit this issue to syntactic fake tool-call text and leave natural-language success claims or mandatory validator policies to the broader response-gate tracking item.

recommendation.title: Define bounded enforcement
recommendation.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it with focused agent-loop, provider-stream, Gateway, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a core agent-runtime security/default behavior decision, and this handle has the strongest current history on fake-tool diagnostics and explicit tool-call terminal policy.
